title: Etale morphisms are locally of finite presentation
statement:
An etale morphism of schemes is locally of finite presentation; hence
an etale morphism $U\to X$ which is quasi-compact, with $X$ of
finite type over a field $K$, has $U$ of finite type over $K$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], an étale morphism $U\to X$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type (over affine opens a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated). Since $X$ is of finite type over $K$, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type by the finite-type clause of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The composite $U\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is quasi-compact, because a composite of quasi-compact morphisms is quasi-compact (the preimage of an affine open is quasi-compact, hence a finite union of affine opens, each with quasi-compact preimage; Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_comp, Morphisms/QuasiCompact.lean:69), and it is locally of finite type, because a composite of morphisms locally of finite type is locally of finite type (on affine opens, a finitely generated algebra over a finitely generated algebra is finitely generated; Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_comp, Morphisms/FiniteType.lean:68). Therefore the composite is of finite type by the clause of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] identifying finite type with quasi-compact and locally of finite type.
